author: lukasmasuch
body:
## Describe your changes

Tornado changed the logic on how `websocket_ping_interval` and `websocket_ping_timeout` are handled. With the latest version, the `websocket_ping_interval` can never be less than the `websocket_ping_timeout`. This leads to an unexpected ping timeout of 1s when the current Streamlit is using the latest tornado version. To fix this, we are updating the `websocket_ping_interval` to use 30s (suggestion from Tornado maintainer https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/pull/3376#issuecomment-2987096711)

This could potentially bring back an old issue with dropping connections in specific proxy setups - https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3196. Something we need to watch out for after this gets released. 

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11670

## Testing Plan

- Added unit test.

body:
# Lambda Diagnostics Workflow for Login Handler Debugging

## Purpose
Add a GitHub Actions workflow to capture Lambda logs and diagnose the 502 "Internal server error" occurring in the login handler after the recent CORS fixes.

## What This PR Does
- ✅ Adds `.github/workflows/lambda-diagnose.yml` workflow
- ✅ Uses repo secrets (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION) for AWS CLI access
- ✅ Manually triggered workflow with configurable duration (default 5 minutes)
- ✅ Tails `/aws/lambda/loginHandler` logs in real-time during execution
- ✅ Captures both live logs and filters recent ERROR patterns
- ✅ Uploads logs as downloadable artifacts for analysis

## Workflow Features
- **AWS Connection Verification**: Tests AWS CLI connection and lists available log groups
- **Real-time Log Tailing**: Captures live Lambda logs during specified duration
- **Error Pattern Filtering**: Identifies recent ERROR logs from Lambda execution
- **Artifact Upload**: Makes captured logs downloadable for analysis

## Usage
1. Trigger workflow manually from GitHub Actions tab
2. During the log capture window, perform login attempt at production URL
3. Download captured logs from workflow run artifacts
4. Analyze stack trace to identify root cause of 502 error

## Context
This workflow is part of the investigation into the student login 502 error that persists after resolving CORS issues. The Lambda function appears to be failing during runtime, and this workflow will capture the specific stack trace needed to identify and fix the root cause.

**Link to Devin run**: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f289c2a2456f4ede9f0ee0290834fccd
**Requested by**: Nathan Walker (nwalker@brightbotsint.com)

author: fw-bot
body: Steps to reproduce : 1) Install the Purchase module 2) Create and confirm a Purchase Order with a product and quantity 3) From the Purchase Order, open the product and archive it Issue: Before archiving the product, the `Purchased` smart button correctly displays the total purchased quantity. However, after archiving the product template, this smart button displays `0.0`, even though purchases exist. Additionally, clicking the button opens a blank purchase order line view instead of showing related records if the product is archived. Cause:- Archiving a product template sets active=False on the template and its variants. The computed field `purchased_product_qty` relies on the variants to calculate the total. Because the variants are inactive post-archival, the compute method sees no records, resulting in a displayed value of 0.0. Similarly, the smart button action uses the active variants in its domain, so it fails to find any related purchase order lines. Solution: The context is now explicitly set with active_test=False when computing the purchased_product_qty and when generating the domain for the smart button action. This ensures that even inactive variants are included in the calculation and the view logic, preserving the correct purchased quantity and showing the relevant purchase lines after archival. opw-4781578 Forward-Port-Of: odoo/odoo#213484 Forward-Port-Of: odoo/odoo#209955

author: tejasgarg
body:
Fixes: #37 

I have started implementing an Interrupt-based UART driver that uses DMA and DMA-based interrupts to function.
This is not yet complete, and I will be working over the next couple of days to make it fully functional.

I also plan to implement a timeout feature, which will make this overall system more reliable. 

Currently, it initialises the DMA for uart module, sets up the NVIC, the callback functions and the IRQ handler.
I have added the read and write functions for the DMA module.
I am yet to properly initialise the NVIC priority and sub-priority for the DMA module, and will also be setting that up.

I plan to also add some form of test case, either in the main file or the UART file, to test if this is working.
It will work by sending a transmitter buffer that I have already initialised in the UART file, by connecting the tx pin[D8] using a jumper cable to the rx pin[D9], over to the receiver buffer using DMA over UART.

## Summary by Sourcery

Implement an interrupt-driven UART driver using DMA on USART3 by adding DMA init functions, non-blocking APIs, NVIC configuration, and IRQ handlers, and integrate these changes into system startup and the main application loop while updating the build configuration.

New Features:
- Add DMA initialization routines for USART3 RX and TX channels
- Introduce usart3_dma_read and usart3_dma_write APIs for DMA-driven UART transfers
- Convert UART_read and UART_write to use interrupt-based (IT) calls instead of blocking mode

Enhancements:
- Configure NVIC priorities and enable IRQs for USART3 and its DMA channels
- Add IRQ handlers for USART3 and GPDMA1 channels to dispatch HAL interrupt callbacks
- Integrate DMA setup and status reporting into system initialization
- Update main loop to use DMA-based read/write and demonstrate echo logic over DMA

Build:
- Link HAL DMA, DMAEx, USART, and UARTEx modules in CMakeLists.txt
- Enable HAL_USART_MODULE in HAL configuration header

author: copilot
body:
This PR fixes an issue where interactive sketch components were visible immediately in `workshop.html`, unlike in `index.html` where they are properly hidden until the "Load Interactives" button is clicked.

## Problem
In `workshop.html`, the CSS rule `.workshop-section .sketch` had `display: flex` which overrode the base CSS rule `.sketch { display: none; }`. This caused sketches to appear immediately on page load, showing empty sketch canvases before user interaction.

## Solution
Modified `paper/viz/workshop.css` to:
1. Change `.workshop-section .sketch` to have `display: none` initially (matching the intended behavior)
2. Add a new rule `.workshop-section .sketch[style*="display: block"]` with `display: flex !important` to ensure proper flex layout when JavaScript activates the sketches

## Changes
- **Modified**: `paper/viz/workshop.css` (1 line changed, 4 lines added)
- **No changes** to HTML files or JavaScript functionality

## Testing
✅ Workshop sketches are now hidden initially  
✅ Workshop sketches display correctly when "Load Interactives" is clicked  
✅ Index.html functionality remains unchanged  
✅ Both pages now have consistent behavior  

The fix ensures surgical precision with minimal changes while preserving all existing functionality.

Fixes #124.

author: cecileane
body:
new features:
- The `NamedTuple` returned by `plot` now includes the coordinates of arrows.
  For logic, these extra slots are not placed at the end, which technically causes an API change (items previously 13 & 14 are now in positions 17 & 18).
  But this change is considered minor enough to *not* warrant a change in the package major version, because: (1) the plot itself if the output of interest, not the returned NamedTuple (2) this output NamedTuple should be accessed by names, and there is *no* API change when doing so.
- new option `preorder`: to make it possible to avoid re-directing edges and re-calculating node pre-ordering
- new options: `edgelabeladj`, `nodelabeladj`, `defaultedgecolor`
- new option: `edgecolor` as a dictionary

bug fixes
- `edgewidth`s were not used for minor hybrid edges (arrows); they now are
- output node and edge data frame without `undef` values. Previously, their `lab` column had undefined values, and subsetting the data frame or its `lab` column lead to: `ERROR: UndefRefError: access to undefined reference`. Associated tests were added.
